2O.1 We are required to give thanks to God.
2O.9 Give thanks always for all things to God.

precepts.text: It is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves. Nobody consulted us about where to put the knee or what colour skin to give us.
precepts.point: Pride is hateful before God and man. You can repent and hop back to the right side, but on the side of pride you are on the side God hates, and everything he hates has an expiration date.
precepts.why:
“Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.” Pride, arrogance, disdain, the inability to admit fault, the inflated ego: God said it wasn't made for you. You are nothing but dust that shall return to where it came from. And anger doesn't get you anywhere either; it holds you back and stunts your growth.

Why wasn't pride made for us? “Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves”. You didn't put one finger on your hand. You didn't put the knee bone with the hip bone and the leg bone. All of that belongs to God, the Creator, from way back when he said, Let us make man in our image.

He didn't consult you: where should I put the knee? How high up on the leg should it go? What should the arch of the foot look like? What skin tone should I give them? What should I make their hair like? None of us were included in that conversation.

So pride has no ground to stand on. The one who did not make himself cannot be proud before the one who made him. That is why the beginning of pride is turning away from your Maker.

precepts.text: The Most High knew us and formed us in the belly before we came forth.
precepts.point: That He made us and not we ourselves goes with the Most High forming us in the belly and knowing us before we were born.

note.label: Psalm 100: Make a Joyful Noise Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.” That he made us and not we ourselves goes with the Most High forming us in the belly and knowing us before we were born.

He said it to Jeremiah: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.” The Most High knew us and formed us in the belly before we came forth. We did not make ourselves; he formed us, and he knew us before the womb.

That is why we are his people and the sheep of his pasture, and why all lands are to serve him with gladness and come before his presence with singing.

precepts.text: The righteousness of the Most High is an everlasting righteousness and His law is the truth.
precepts.point: The Most High is good, His mercy is everlasting, and His truth endures to all generations. That truth is His laws, which endure to all generations.

note.label: Psalm 100: Make a Joyful Noise Unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“For the Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.” That truth is his laws, which endure to all generations.

David says what the truth is: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” His law is the truth, and his righteousness is everlasting, just as his mercy is everlasting.

So the truth that endures to all generations is the law of the Most High. Enter his gates with thanksgiving and bless his name for it.

points: All lands are to make a joyful noise unto the Most High and serve Him with gladness, coming before His presence with singing.
